fields.name: Memory Timing Mode
fields.danger: Codes beyond 0 are not established. The upstream project this derives from uses 0/1/2 for AUTO/CUSTOM/NO adjust; 4IFIR renamed them and added a fourth, so the order is a guess. Writing a wrong code here changes how the whole timing subsystem behaves. Read-only until the author confirms.
fields.help_text: Selects how the firmware handles the memory timing table as a whole. Left alone: the value in every shipped kip is 0, meaning automatic.
fields.help_source: CustomizeTable source; mode codes from the upstream OC Toolkit example

fields.name: CPU Boost Clock
fields.help_text: CPU Boost Mode controls the maximum possible CPU frequency, used by system in boost mode (game loadings, tinfoil downloads, etc.)

menu_path.ebal: Ebal > Tuning > ProTools > Cpu > [*CPU Boost Clock]

fields.name: RAM Vdd2
fields.help_text: Main memory voltage. Normally it comes from the EMC Balance mode together with the memory speed — this item overrides it with a fixed figure. Higher is not better: it is heat and wear for stability you may already have. If you are unsure, leave it and change EMC Balance instead.
fields.help_source: CustomizeTable source + operator, 2026-08-14

fields.name: CPU Voltage Limit
fields.help_text:
This menu allows you to set the maximum allowable CPU voltage. 

The higher the voltage, the higher the maximum available processor frequency, but the higher the consumption. 

It is recommended to increase it if there is a lack of maximum frequency for processor-intensive games.

menu_path.ebal: Ebal > Tuning > ProTools > Cpu > [*CPU Max Voltage?erista]

fields.name: RAM MHz
fields.help_text: Memory speed on Erista. Left on automatic, the firmware picks the mode from your memory chip and steps down if the banks do not hold it. Setting a figure here overrides that choice. The voltages the mode needs follow from EMC Balance, not from this item.
fields.help_source: CustomizeTable source + operator, 2026-08-14

fields.name: CPU Maximum Voltage
fields.help_text:
CPU VMAX mode controls the max voltage available to the CPU by the system.

The higher value- the more power can be drawn by the CPU, and the higher frequencies it can reach.

To test this setting - run the CPU-heavy game and see if the performance is goodon the max CPU load.

menu_path.ebal: Ebal > Tuning > ProTools > Cpu > [*CPU Max Voltage?mariko]

fields.name: RAM MHz
fields.help_text: Memory speed on Mariko. Left on automatic, the firmware picks the mode from your memory chip and steps down if the banks do not hold it — so two consoles with the same chip can end up on different speeds. Setting a figure here overrides that choice. The voltages the mode needs follow from EMC Balance, not from this item; raise the speed and you may have to give the memory more.
fields.help_source: CustomizeTable source + operator, 2026-08-14

fields.name: RAM Vddq
fields.help_text: Memory bus voltage (Vddq). Like Vdd2, it normally follows from the EMC Balance mode and the memory speed; this item pins it to a fixed figure. Too low and the console will not boot; on some builds it has been reported to damage an emuNAND, so step carefully.
fields.help_source: CustomizeTable source + operator, 2026-08-14

fields.name: Low MHz Undervolt
fields.help_text:
This menu allows you to set undervolting mode for frequencies from 16XX MHz and down.

The higher the value, the more agressive undervolting is appied to the CPU.

menu_path.ebal: Ebal > Tuning > ProTools > Cpu > [CPU Low MHz UV: ]

fields.name: GPU Undervolt Mode
fields.name_fixed: Was "768MHz" — a curve point name stuck to this field while merging sources: in the original packages the 44=03 gate was written as a side effect from every point. Per customize.cpp:72 this is marikoGpuUV.

fields.name: CPU Minimal Voltage
fields.help_text: Auto steps let the kip pick the floor. A fixed value in mV switches the automation off - then you raise it yourself by 20 mV for every extra 200 MHz of RAM.

menu_path.ebal: Ebal > Tuning > ProTools > Cpu > [*CPU Min Voltage]

fields.name: GPU Minimal Voltage

menu_path.ebal: Ebal > Tuning > ProTools > Gpu > [*GPU Min Voltage]

fields.help_text: Lets the kip work out the GPU voltage floor for each RAM speed on its own. Fine-tune it with the two vMin Offset items below.

fields.name: Core Timings 1
fields.help_text: Sets tRCD - the delay between opening a row and reading from it. The value picks a position in the table of tRCD values by memory frequency. Higher values tighten the timing, which gives more performance and less margin. The eBal mode is part of the formula, so changing eBal moves this timing too.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: Core Timings 2
fields.help_text: Sets tRP - the delay before a new row can be opened after closing one. Higher values tighten the timing, which gives more performance and less margin. The eBal mode is part of the formula, so changing eBal moves this timing too. The top value here is not simply the most aggressive: it switches to a separate algorithm.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: Core Timings 3
fields.help_text: Sets tRAS - how long a row must stay open before it may be closed. This one is twice as sensitive to the eBal mode as the first two: eBal enters its formula with a factor of two. Higher values tighten the timing, which gives more performance and less margin. The eBal mode is part of the formula, so changing eBal moves this timing too.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: Core Timings 4
fields.help_text: Sets tRFC - the recovery time after a refresh. The exact formula is not documented by the firmware author; only that this item controls it. Higher values tighten the timing, which gives more performance and less margin. The eBal mode is part of the formula, so changing eBal moves this timing too.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: Core Timings 5
fields.help_text: Which timing this one sets has not been established - the firmware documentation leaves that row empty. What is known for certain: it acts IN SUM with Core Timings 1, so raising this one also raises the first. Move it only after the first is where you want it.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: Core Timings 6
fields.help_text: Sets tWTR - the gap between a write and a following read. Each step removes two cycles. Besides eBal, this timing depends on the memory voltage Vdd2: more voltage allows more. Higher values tighten the timing, which gives more performance and less margin. The eBal mode is part of the formula, so changing eBal moves this timing too.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: Core Timings 7
fields.help_text: Sets tRTW - the gap between a read and a following write. Each step removes two cycles, and it also depends on the memory voltage Vdd2. Higher values tighten the timing, which gives more performance and less margin. The eBal mode is part of the formula, so changing eBal moves this timing too.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: EMC Balance
fields.help_text: EMC Balance — the trade between memory speed and how hard the memory is pushed. It is also what decides the voltages your memory runs at by default: each level of this setting maps to its own Vdd2 for the current speed. Lower levels press for efficiency and want more voltage; higher levels lean toward frequency and want less. Change this before touching Vdd2 or Vddq by hand.
fields.help_source: CustomizeTable source + operator, 2026-08-14

fields.name: Core Timings 8
fields.help_text: Sets tWTP - the gap between a write and precharge. The only timing that EBA-Shift takes part in: the smaller the distance between eBal and EBA-Shift, the further this one can go. Higher values tighten the timing, which gives more performance and less margin. The eBal mode is part of the formula, so changing eBal moves this timing too.
fields.help_source: semantics-src/ram.json, derived from the firmware source

fields.name: pMeh 0 eBAS Sub-Zero
fields.help_text: pMeh 0 eBAS Sub-Zero - Derived from eBAL: eBAS, eBAW and eBAR. eBAS can be increased using the [eba-shift] option. The only way to decrease it is by using — pMeh[0] and only by 1 (when set to pmeh[0]=1)
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 0 eBAS Sub-Zero.txt

fields.name: pMeh 1 divMB Supressor
fields.help_text: pMeh 1 divMB Supressor - Affects the stability of the frequency step if it is unstable without clear reasons. Remember those non-working frequencies like 2800? They are probably gone, but if you find any, try toggling this switch.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 1 divMB Supressor.txt

fields.help_text: pMeh 13 DR Debug - Disables 4ifir optimizations. In the first mode, it eliminates the least critical optimizations from the list of potential culprits for all problems. In the second mode - more critical ones, etc.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 13 DR Debug.txt

fields.name: pMeh 14 GameChanger
fields.help_text: pMeh 14 GameChanger - soon
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 14 GameChanger.txt

fields.name: pMeh 15 eFOS MK
fields.help_text: pMeh 15 eFOS MK - increases the delay that occurs when switching from one memory mode to another (e.g., switching from EMC - 4ifir optimised to EMC - 4ifir optimised S).
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 15 eFOS MK.txt

fields.name: pMeh 16 lovec
fields.help_text: pMeh 16 lovec - Reduces system timings performance
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 16 lovec.txt

fields.name: pMeh 17 WL-Set
fields.help_text: Write Latency Set, range 0-1. The original packages label this item DBI with four values — that is out of date: DBI moved to sMeh 17, and this offset now holds something else. Undocumented beyond the name, so leave it at 0 unless you know why.
fields.help_source: customize.cpp (current revision) — renamed from the label both donor packages still use

fields.name: pMeh 18 eBAMATIC ST
fields.help_text: pMeh 18 eBAMATIC ST - selects the eBamatic optimization level. The higher the value, the more aggressive the optimization. (Duplicate of item QuickTune > eBAMATIC > e.BAMATIC Stage)
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 18 eBAMATIC ST.txt

fields.name: pMeh 19 vMINetune ST

menu_path.ebal: (МЁРТВЫЙ, только через Expert/MiniPackage) 4IFIR Optimized Setup > [*pMeh 19 vMINetune ST]

fields.platform_source: pMEH[19] vMINetune ST — Ebal GPU.ini:99 | 29.08.2026: снята пометка mariko — в оригинальном 4IFIR Wizard оба поля лежат в RAM > MICRO-ENHANCE LOGIC без фильтра платформы и видны на обеих ревизиях, и его сброс к заводским пишет в них безусловно. Решение оператора: как в оригинале.
fields.help_text: Shifts the automatic GPU voltage floor for Optimized E RAM. This is a shift, not the voltage itself: plus raises it, minus lowers it. Step is 5 mV.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 19 vMINetune ST.txt
fields.range_note: ДИАПАЗОН РАСШИРЕН АВТОРОМ ПРОШИВКИ ПО ПРОСЬБЕ. Строка-легенда в customize.cpp говорит «0-9», но это устаревший комментарий: Cooler3D добавил значения выше и ниже по личной просьбе оператора. Все 15 пунктов рабочие. НЕ ОБРЕЗАТЬ по легенде.

fields.name: pMeh 20 rVDDick
fields.help_text: pMeh 20 rVDDick - VDDQ/VDD2 for 4ifir Optimised (The higher the value, the higher the voltage)
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/pMeh 20 rVDDick.txt

fields.range_note: ДИАПАЗОН РАСШИРЕН АВТОРОМ ПРОШИВКИ ПО ПРОСЬБЕ. Строка-легенда в customize.cpp говорит «0-9», но это устаревший комментарий: Cooler3D добавил значения выше и ниже по личной просьбе оператора. Все 15 пунктов рабочие. НЕ ОБРЕЗАТЬ по легенде.

fields.name: pMeh 22 isKefir
fields.help_text: Range 0-1. Present in the current firmware structure but not documented beyond its name; both original packages predate it and never exposed it. Leave at 0 unless you know why you are changing it.
fields.help_source: customize.cpp (актуальная ревизия)

fields.name: sMeh 0 ARB-Boost

fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 1 ARB-BCD.txt

fields.name: sMeh 2 ARB-BRP
fields.help_text: sMeh 2 ARB-BRP - Allow, without affecting stability, in certain combinations of timings, eBALs and frequencies, where 4IFIR was not included algorithmically with 100% arbitration timings by memory controllers, to adjust them manually.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 2 ARB-BRP.txt

fields.name: sMeh 3 ARB-RTR
fields.help_text: sMeh 3 ARB-RTR - Allow, without affecting stability, in certain combinations of timings, eBALs and frequencies, where 4IFIR was not included algorithmically with 100% arbitration timings by memory controllers, to adjust them manually.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 3 ARB-RTR.txt

fields.name: sMeh 4 ARB-RTW
fields.help_text: sMeh 4 ARB-RTW - Allow, without affecting stability, in certain combinations of timings, eBALs and frequencies, where 4IFIR was not included algorithmically with 100% arbitration timings by memory controllers, to adjust them manually.

fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 6 eZQ Override.txt

fields.name: sMeh 7 trDVFS
fields.help_text: sMeh 7 trDVFS - soon
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 7 trDVFS.txt

menu_path.ebal: (МЁРТВЫЙ, только через Expert/MiniPackage) 4IFIR Optimized Setup > [*sMeh 8 E-Boost]

fields.help_text: sMeh 8 E-Boost - Memory efficiency stages in Optimized E mode. The higher the value, the more performance. Because of sMeh 8, the screen may start to stripe in the dock. To solve this problem, reset sMeh 8 to 0.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 8 E-Boost.txt

fields.name: sMeh 9 SSC Logic
fields.help_text: sMeh 9 SSC Logic - switches between two modes of operation of the RAM clock generator noise suppressor. It can help if something wireless at certain RAM frequencies behaves strangely.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 9 SSC Logic.txt

fields.name: sMeh 10 Latent
fields.help_text: sMeh 10 - soon
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 10 Latent.txt

fields.name: sMeh 11 REF-NEH
fields.help_text: sMeh 11 - soon
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 11 REF-NEH.txt

fields.name: sMeh 12 Clatok
fields.help_text: sMeh 12 Clatok - Switches between algorithms for scaling technical, engineering parameters and memory timings, between two principles. Mode 1, in most cases, should give a gain of a couple of FPS under equal conditions.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 12 Clatok.txt

fields.name: sMeh 13 CPriora
fields.help_text: sMeh 13 CPriora - CPU priority. Reduces performance per megahertz for GPU in favor of CPU. Ideal for emulators.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 13 CPriora.txt

fields.name: sMeh 14 GetLow
fields.help_text: sMeh 14 GetLow - Control the degree of aggressiveness of the zero-jump algorithm, also known as 4VOLTSHIFT. The more aggressive, the faster the memory will switch to the lower mode, at the cost of an increased risk of not making it.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 14 GetLow.txt

fields.name: sMeh 15 GetHigh
fields.help_text: sMeh 15 GetHigh - Control the degree of aggressiveness of the zero-jump algorithm, also known as 4VOLTSHIFT. The more aggressive, the faster the memory will switch to the upper mode, at the cost of an increased risk of not making it.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 15 GetHigh.txt

fields.name: sMeh 16 SYK-LOH

menu_path.ebal: (МЁРТВЫЙ, только через Expert/MiniPackage) 4IFIR Optimized Setup > [*sMeh 16 SYK-LOH]

fields.help_text: sMeh 16 SYK-LOH - Sets the value RAM Optimized - 1600 MHz.
fields.help_source: 4IFIR Wizard Help/sMeh 16 SYK-LOH.txt

fields.name: sMeh 17 DBI
fields.help_text: Data Bus Inversion, range 0-3. In older firmware this sat in the pMeh array; it moved here, and both original packages still write it to the old place. Undocumented beyond the name.
